summary.name: Superagent
summary.one_liner: Superagent is a security platform that runs built-in security features against repositories, web apps, and AI agents, routes findings into development workflows, and keeps human approval on consequential changes.
keywords: monitor or block risky agent actions
use_cases: reviewing pull requests for code, workflow, dependency, and contributor risk before merge
generating dependency update pull requests that pass package policy
running red team assessments against repositories and deployed web apps
testing deployed agents and applying runtime guardrails
monitoring or blocking risky actions taken by AI agents
summary.what_it_does: Superagent connects software targets (repositories, applications, agents, and planned infrastructure) to built-in security features. Its features include PR Security for reviewing code, workflow, dependency, and contributor risk before merge; Secure Dependency Updates for generating dependency update pull requests that pass package policy; Red Team for finding and reproducing attack paths; and Agent Guardrails for checking what agents consume and monitoring or blocking risky actions. Findings are routed into the user's development workflow, and structured reviewed results are retained as context for later runs. Schedules and integrations control when work runs and where results go. The page describes installing a Superagent skill for coding agents via npx.
notable: Pull request security review and dependency update PRs that must pass package policy
Browser-based red team assessments of deployed web surfaces and agents
Runtime guardrails that monitor or block risky agent actions
Installable skill for coding agents via npx skills add superagent-ai/skills
caveats: Infrastructure coverage (developer machines, agent hosts, CI runners, cloud workloads) is listed as coming soon
